headline: High: Devin’s broad write/network/OAuth autonomy can create dangerous interaction paths, while godot_rl_agents is mostly inert and local-only.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests external content through browsers, MCP, Slack, GitHub, and files, so prompt injection is plausible if it reads attacker-controlled text. godot_rl_agents has no documented I/O surfaces or output channel, so it is not itself an injection source; the pair risk comes from Devin’s permissive parsers and shared integrations, not from B.
conditions: IF Devin reads untrusted repo, issue, Slack, or MCP content as instructions
IF an attacker can place text into a shared integration that Devin processes
mitigations: Restrict Devin to trusted repositories and channels for the session
Disable or narrow MCP servers for the run
Require a human review step before executing instructions found in files or messages
Use a separate workspace for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for integration-fed text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens, so leakage risk exists if sensitive data enters its cloud workspace. godot_rl_agents shows no data classes or I/O surfaces, so it is not a direct exfiltration path; the pair risk is mainly Devin’s outbound integrations and cloud processing.
conditions: IF sensitive source code, chat, or tokens are placed in Devin’s workspace
IF Devin is connected to external integrations that receive its context or outputs
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in Devin’s workspace
Rotate any tokens used during the session
Limit Devin to non-sensitive repositories
Review integration permissions before launch
requires-engineering: enforce redaction on outbound context

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has broad write and git capabilities, but godot_rl_agents has no documented write, network, or workspace-sharing capability, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. The only plausible conflict is if an operator manually couples them through shared files or a repo, which is unusual and not default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable repository or directory
IF an operator manually bridges outputs into a shared git workflow
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not share a mutable repo between them
Use branch protection and lock discipline
Run godot_rl_agents read-only if it is ever connected to files
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can produce code, docs, and integration actions, but godot_rl_agents has no documented downstream action-taking authority or input channel, so there is no default chain where B blindly executes A’s output. Any cascade would require an external orchestrator to feed Devin’s outputs into B, which is not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external workflow passes Devin’s outputs into godot_rl_agents as authoritative input
IF a human or orchestrator skips verification between the agents
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Do not auto-forward Devin outputs into B
Keep B isolated from code-generation outputs
Log and review any handoff payloads
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Devin is a closed-source cloud workspace agent that handles source code, chat, and integration tokens, while godot_rl_agents is open-source and appears local/simulation-oriented with no data classes. The main compliance issue is residency or retention mismatch if regulated data is sent to Devin; B is not cited further because it shows no relevant residency or retention surface.
conditions: IF regulated data such as customer secrets or personal data is processed in Devin’s cloud workspace
IF organizational policy requires local-only processing for the touched data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Devin
Confirm retention settings for connected integrations
Use synthetic or masked data
Document the data flow before deployment
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or residency-approved deployment
